subject: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls discussion
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finserv.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@finserv.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls discussion

Hi Sarah and Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. As promised, I wanted to recap the key data/privacy items we discussed and propose next steps so we can keep momentum on the procurement side. Key points from our call: 

- Scope: You confirmed that PII (customer names, account numbers, limited transaction metadata) will be sent to Redwood for inference only; no raw payment card data.
- Data residency: Primary requirement is US-only storage for customer data; EU residency may be needed for a subset in the future.
- Retention: You expect short retention for inference artifacts (24–72 hours) and longer retention for audit logs (12 months).
- Access controls: Must support RBAC, least privilege for support, time-limited break-glass, and logged support sessions with approver audit.
- Logging/audit: You need immutable audit logs for all data access and a way to export them for your compliance team.

Attachments: I attached a short SOC2 summary and our RBAC role set for reference. Also linking our RBAC overview: https://redwood.inference/docs/security/rbac 

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Rishi + Neha and your security engineer to review RBAC, break-glass flow, and audit exports — can we do Wed 3/4 or Thu 3/5?
2) I’ll share a concise mutual action plan (MAP) and the security questionnaire you requested.
3) If all good, we’ll prepare a short demo of the support access break-glass flow in a sandbox environment.

Please confirm who from your security/compliance team should attend the technical call and which date/time works best.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: SOC2-Summary.pdf (stub), RBAC-roles.csv (stub)

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finserv.com>

Date: 2026-03-01T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls discussion

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Break-glass: We require an approver outside of the Redwood support org (our on-call security lead) to explicitly approve elevation requests; time-limited to a max of 4 hours per incident.
- Support access: Any support session that touches PII must be recorded and have an immutable audit trail.
- Retention: For audit logs we need a retention of 12 months, immutable, with export capability to our S3.

We can do the technical deep-dive on Thu 3/5 at 11:00 AM PT. Our security lead (Tom) will attend and security@finserv.com will be on the call.

Sarah Jones
Head of Security Operations
FinServ Bank

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & access controls discussion

Adding a few technical clarifications ahead of Thu's call: 

- RBAC: We support fine-grained roles (viewer, analyst, ops-support, escalations-admin). We can map your internal roles to these and create tenant-scoped roles so Redwood support cannot access customer PII unless elevated.
- Least privilege & time-limited sessions: Break-glass is implemented as a scoped elevation token (issued after approver authorization). Token duration configurable; default 1 hour, can be set to max 4 hours per policy.
- Support session logging: All support sessions produce an immutable audit record (who, when, scope, justification) and we capture a session transcript/record that can be exported to your S3 bucket via secure transfer.
- Audit immutability: Logs are write-once and checksummed; retention policy supports 12+ months and export in JSON/CSV.

I'll bring a runbook and a short diagram showing the approval flow and where logs are stored. If you can confirm the S3 export target format (JSON vs CSV) and whether you prefer encrypted-at-rest keys managed by you (KMS) or Redwood-managed, we'll include that in the MAP.

Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai)

Thanks — couple more items to validate before Thu: 

1) Data residency: For now we need US-only at rest and in transit; is that supported for both inference artifacts and logs? Please confirm whether Redwood will guarantee no cross-region replicas of logs without explicit opt-in.
2) Demo environment: We'd like a sandbox where we can send representative PII (anonymized) and see the break-glass flow end-to-end.

If you can confirm 1) and confirm the sandbox is possible, we'll provide a small test payload.

Tom
Security Engineer | FinServ Bank

Tom — quick answers: 

1) Data residency: Yes — we can enforce US-only storage for both inference artifacts and logs. We will not create cross-region replicas unless explicitly enabled in the tenant config. I'll document that in the MAP.
2) Sandbox: Absolutely — we'll provision a sandbox tenant scoped to FinServ with anonymized PII. Rishi/Neha will demo the break-glass flow and produce audit exports to your S3 target during the call. Please share the preferred S3 output format and whether you want to use your KMS keys or Redwood-managed keys.

Next steps recap (Thu 3/5, 11:00 AM PT):
- Technical deep-dive + runbook demo (Rishi/Neha)
